title: Stock Market Today Highlights, September 9: Sensex crashes 813 pts, Nifty closes at 23,431 as crude prices cross $100 - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights - Find here all the highlights related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 9th September 2026.

In a sharp escalation of a six-month-old war in the Middle East, ‌Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said it fired ballistic missiles at a base in Jordan used by the ‌U.S. military and attacked 10 ships on Wednesday, ‌after ⁠Washington said it had destroyed five Iranian oil ⁠tankers.

The Nifty 50 fell 0.86% to 23,431.50 and the BSE Sensex lost 1.08% to 74,764.23. Both benchmarks logged their lowest closing levels since June 11.

Other Asian stock ‌markets were subdued, as fresh attacks stoked inflation worries ahead of the release of closely watched U.S. inflation data this week.

Thirteen of the 16 major sectors logged ‌losses.

Rupee fell past the key 95-per-dollar mark ​on Wednesday, as escalating conflict in the Middle East put ‌oil prices back on the boil, prompting likely ​central bank intervention to limit the ⁠South Asian currency’s losses.

Equity benchmarks ended in red for the third straight session. Sensex and Nifty ended at the lowest levels. BSE Sensex tumbled 813.35 pts or 1.08% to 74,764.23. Nifty 50 depreciated 203.60 pts or 0.86% to 23,431.50.

RBI conducts September USD/INR sell-buy swaps as forward premiums rise, signaling changes in rupee liquidity management.

Top gainers of Nifty 50: Adani Enterprises (+4.85%), Max Health (+4.41%), Adani Ports (+3.79%), Coal India (+2.84%)

Top losers: Infosys (-5.06%), HCL Tech (-3.83%), Tech Mahindra (-3.79%), HDFC Life (-3.49%), Wipro (-2.55%)

Sales stood at 104009 units in August 2026 and exports at 6134 units.

Sun Pharma: Sun Pharma Global Treasury Centre IFSC has been incorporated an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of the Company in the International Financial Services Centre at GIFT City, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, India.

The new capability, launched at Global Fintech Fest 2026 in partnership with Juspay, enables businesses to manage multiple payment aggregators through a single integration, with intelligent routing and a unified view of payment performance, refunds and reconciliation. The solution is aimed at helping businesses improve payment resilience and simplify the growing complexity of digital collections.

Karamtara Engineering IPO fully subscribed on Day 1. Sees 1.03 times subscription at 2.45 pm on Sep 9. QIBs: 1.20 times; NIIs: 1.44 times; Retail 0.75 times.

Visa, AU Small Finance Bank, and CheQ unveiled the CheQ AU Credit Card at Global Fintech Fest 2026, showcasing India’s first LED-enabled credit card designed to enhance the contactless payment experience. The card combines AU SFB’s banking expertise, Visa’s global payments network, and CheQ’s consumer-focused platform to deliver a differentiated credit offering.

IOL Chemicals is setting up a fully backward-integrated, state-of-the-art new manufacturing unit for Ibuprofen at its existing site at Barnala, Punjab, with an installed manufacturing capacity of 6,000 MT per annum, which will enhance the Company’s existing Ibuprofen manufacturing capacity from 12,000 MT per annum to 18,000 MT per annum upon commissioning of the new unit.

The Company has installed a new pharmaceutical formulation manufacturing facility at its existing site at Barnala, Punjab, diversifying into Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisation (“CDMO”) for Pharmaceutical Formulations as a new line of business.

The Company is also establishing a dedicated manufacturing facility for the manufacture of the Specialty Chemical Product for a Leading Global Chemical Company under a long-term tolling arrangement. The project entails an estimated capital expenditure of approximately ₹35 Crore, to be funded through internal accruals. The facility will be dedicated to fulfilling the customer’s long-term requirements under the tolling arrangement. The facility is expected to be commercialized during the Q3 FY 2027.

Embassy Developments Limited today announced the appointment of Neel Virwani as Chief Business Officer, effective October 1, 2026, following the approval of his appointment as Senior Management Personnel by the Company’s Board of Directors and shareholders.

A Promoter at Embassy Group and part of its next generation of leadership, Neel has been associated with the Group since April 2024, working across strategic planning, business development, and brand transformation initiatives. He has been instrumental in evaluating new markets and expansion opportunities, while also maintaining close involvement with the Group’s family office and investment activities.

As Chief Business Officer, Neel will lead EDL’s operations across North and West India, with a particular focus on the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) and the National Capital Region (NCR). He will be responsible for driving portfolio expansion, spearheading new business initiatives, and overseeing project structuring and execution across the Company’s owned and development management portfolio.

Kotak Alternate Asset Managers Limited (Kotak Alts) today announced the successful exit from its investment in HKR Roadways Limited through the sale of the company to Cube Highways and Infrastructure V Pte. Limited. The investment was made through Kotak Alts’ Special Situations strategy.

HKR is a special purpose vehicle operating a 206 km four-lane state highway project in Telangana under a Build-Operate-Transfer Toll concession running until February 2041. The asset operates three toll plazas and serves as a critical transportation corridor within Telangana while connecting the state to Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and North India.

Commissioned in 2014, the project faced delays in right-of-way availability, lower-than-expected traffic volumes and sizeable pending capital expenditure. These factors led to debt servicing stress and the asset being classified as a non-performing asset.
